study: Lang et al. 2009, intensive grade-9 reading interventions (READ 180 / REACH / RISE) vs SOAR (JREE)
eval_evidence: Author list includes the program publishers/developers: Scholastic Education (READ 180; C. Chanter) and FL DOE (RISE author E. Lefsky), alongside FSU researchers (Lang, Torgesen, Petscher) and the district (p.90). Developers co-authored/co-ran the evaluation; not an independent third party.
developer_evidence: PD 'conducted by program experts, district literacy coaches, and school-based' staff; specifically the publishers of the two commercial interventions and the author of the third delivered/led the PD (p.244, 527).
cascade_evidence: Program publishers/author provide the teacher PD directly; in-class support is then via a school reading coach assigned to each school. Initial PD is developer-direct (the publishers/author train teachers).
counterfactual_evidence: Control = SOAR (School Offered Accelerated Reading), a school-designed 90-min intensive reading class that also used content-enhancement/reading strategies; an active alternative reading program, not a no-treatment BAU (p.234, 521).
coaching_evidence: A reading coach assigned to each school provided ongoing coaching and feedback to intensive-reading teachers throughout the year, stepping in to model comprehension/vocabulary/self-monitoring strategies (p.242-245, 569).
student_dose_evidence: All four conditions (3 programs + SOAR control) were delivered as a 90-min daily reading block replacing electives; the extra instructional dose is held constant across treatment and control, so no differential added dose for the TPD-vs-control contrast (p.239).
maturity_evidence: Impact year 2006-07 was Year 3 of the project; 28 of 31 teachers were implementing the same program they taught in Year 2, and 'all but 3 teachers had a full-year professional development and experience with the specific curriculum' before the impact year (p.513-521).
